Subject: Follow-up: unit economics / pricing details from today's call

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and the asks we committed to:

1) Your stated goals: embed multi-turn summarization + KYC assistant into the onboarding flow; target response latency <400ms P95; strong cost sensitivity for scale.
2) Expected traffic: you mentioned pilot of ~10k monthly active users with ~15 requests/user/day average and ~200 tokens per request (est). That maps to ~30M tokens/month for pilot and ~1B tokens/month at scale (per your roadmap). Please confirm if those numbers look right.
3) Budget guidance: you said the team is aiming for <$10k/month in inference spend for the pilot and <$50k/month at scale — again, confirm.

Next steps we promised:
- Send a quick unit-economics sketch (attached) showing $/1M tokens at different tiers and an example $/feature breakdown.
- Outline pricing tiers and potential discounts tied to committed volume.
- Provide an SOW template and timeline for a 6–8 week pilot.

Attached: redwood_unit_econ_calc.xlsx (unit econ sketch), redwood_pricing_tiers.pdf, SOW-draft-FintechX.pdf

If you can confirm the token volumes and the budget targets above we’ll return an updated line-item view by Monday.

Thanks —
Marissa

Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the attachments. Numbers below are our best current estimates:

- Pilot (Q2): ~10k MAU, ~12–18 requests/user/day, avg ~180–220 tokens/request -> conservatively 30M tokens/month.
- Ramp (Q3–Q4): we expect 3–4x growth, target 120–150M tokens/month by end of year.
- Long-term (next 12 months): target ~1B tokens/month but that is contingent on product-market fit.

Budget: pilot budget is flexible but ideally <$12k/month. For ramp we'd target <$60k/month.

One additional ask: we need a simple $/feature view so our PM can evaluate margin impact per user feature (e.g., onboarding summary = X tokens per user, KYC chat = Y tokens per user). Can you include an example mapping in the econ sketch?

Also copying Priya and procurement — they’ll want the SOW and a sense of billing terms.

—Alex
VP Product, FintechX
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: unit economics / pricing details from today's call

Alex —

Appreciate the detail. A few quick clarifications and a worked example so your PM can map features to cost:

Assumptions we used in the attached calc:
- Model: small LLM variant for summarization/chat (Redwood-curated 7B quantized).
- Avg tokens/request: 200 (you provided 180–220 so we used mid).
- We assume 30% effective caching/prefix reuse for onboarding flows which reduces billable tokens for repeated requests.
- Our list price (public hosted) for that workload in the sheet = $0.95 / 1M input tokens + $3.50 / 1M output tokens (example blended $/1M shows $4.45). With batching and caching on a Dedicated plan discounts apply.

Worked example (pilot):
- 10k MAU * 15 req/user/day * 200 tokens = 30,000,000 tokens/month
- At blended $4.45 / 1M tokens = ~$133.5 / month (this is illustrative; blended calc picks input+output split).

That number looks obviously low — because the above is per-1M scaling: 30M * 4.45 = $133.5 (note: verify units in the attached sheet).

Feature-level mapping (sample rows in the sheet):
- Onboarding summary (1 request per user, avg 500 tokens) = 0.5M tokens / 1k users -> convert to $/feature.
- KYC assistant (3 messages per onboarding cycle, avg 120 tokens each) = 0.36M tokens / 1k users.

CAC/payback notes:
- If your CAC is $60 and LTV target is 3x, you need per-user gross margin > $40.
- If inference cost per active user (monthly) is $0.13 (pilot numbers), you have a lot of room; but at scale with richer prompts and higher output tokens that can increase to $X. The calc highlights sensitivity to output token length.

We included a sensitivity tab in redwood_unit_econ_calc.xlsx showing $/1M at different quantization & discount levels (hosted vs dedicated vs committed).

Happy to jump on a short call with your PM to walk the sheet.

—Aditya
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up: unit economics / pricing details from today's call

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for confirming volumes and budget. Quick commercial note: we can get you to target economics in two ways depending on your preference:

1) Committed volume (3–6 month) on Redwood Dedicated: aggressive per-1M pricing with a baseline commitment. Example tiers in attached PDF. This is best if you want predictable latency and lower unit cost.
2) Hosted + rate card discounts: faster to start, less commitment, slightly higher $/1M.

Example commitment proposal (illustrative):
- Pilot commit: 30M tokens/month guaranteed for 3 months -> pricing = $3.2 / 1M blended -> monthly inference ~$96.
- Ramp commit: 150M tokens/month guaranteed -> pricing = $2.1 / 1M blended -> monthly inference ~$315.
- For enterprise SOW we can include overage tiers and an optional burst pool.

On margins and CAC payback:
- If your ARPU per customer is $8/mo and CAC is $60, break-even requires 7.5 months of retention. Inference cost at scale (example ramp tier above) per active user/month estimated at $0.26. That gives reasonable margin contribution if product retains users.

Next steps:
- If you want pricing committed for procurement, confirm which path (Dedicated commit vs Hosted).
- If Dedicated, please share target commit window (3/6/12 months) and expected peak tokens. We'll draft a commitment term sheet + SOW.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
